refresh.note: Checked per member: cfr-29 by eCFR api_date; interpretations and publications by URL-set diff; directives by new_identifier - a revised CPL lands under a NEW number, so a hash diff finds nothing.

description: Four layers of one regulatory system, joined on the standard number. cfr-29 is what the rule requires; interpretations are what OSHA says it means; directives are how inspectors enforce it; publications are how to comply. cfr-29 is required because the other three cite it - without it they reference a rule that is not in the corpus.
